newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF mulls new bond reporting rules.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF mulls new bond reporting rules.

text.p: Japan is mulling new rules to require that holdings of certain bonds, such as zero-coupon bonds issued overseas, be reported to the tax authorities, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) tax official said on Thursday.
The move, intended to help prevent tax evasion, is being considered as one part of financial deregulation measures scheduled to be implemented next year, he said.

"We are trying to bring these reporting rules in line with those overseas, particularly in the U.S. and Britain, where the required information is quite specific and often includes identity numbers," the official said.
"By comparison, Japan's reporting rules are quite lax," he added, noting that this could encourage tax evasion, particularly as cross-border transactions pick up.
He said the rules may require the reporting of a bond holder's name, address, and the amount of the securities, although he offered no further details.
This sort of reporting is currently not required for some forms of bonds, including deferred payment and deep-discounted bonds as well as zero coupon bonds, the official said.
He said the matter was currently under study and that a proposal may be submitted to parliament early in 1998.
